## Types

### `mod-id` <Badge type="info" text="type" />

```txt
type mod-id = string;
```

A mod id as written in `mod.toml` (`[a-z0-9_-]{2,40}`).

### `value` <Badge type="info" text="type" />

```txt
type value = list<u8>;
```

A dynamic value crossing a language boundary (service arguments and results, custom event payloads). Always canonical CBOR (RFC 8949 section 4.2.1, "core deterministic encoding"). Records are CBOR maps with kebab-case text keys, variants are one-entry maps `{tag: value}`, enums are text, `option` is null or the value, host handles are `{"$h": u64}`. Each SDK offers typed helpers so authors rarely touch the bytes.

### `pos` <Badge type="info" text="record" />

A tile position in the world. `x` wraps around the world width, `y` grows upwards from bedrock.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | `s32` |  |
| `y` | `s32` |  |

### `side` <Badge type="info" text="enum" />

Which program a piece of mod code runs in.

| Case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `server` | The dedicated server (or the host of a local world). |
| `client` | A game client (PC port or Android loader). |

### `priority` <Badge type="info" text="enum" />

Event handler priority, in Spigot order. Handlers run from `lowest` to `highest`, then `monitor`. Inside one priority they run in mod load order (dependencies first).

| Case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `lowest` | Runs first. Use it when you want later handlers to see and override your decision. |
| `low` | Runs after `lowest`. |
| `normal` | The default. |
| `high` | Runs after `normal`. |
| `highest` | Runs last among handlers that may still cancel or modify the event. |
| `monitor` | Sees the final state. A `monitor` handler can neither cancel nor modify the event; its outcome is ignored. |

### `api-error` <Badge type="info" text="variant" />

Errors returned by host functions.

| Case | Payload | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `not-permitted` | `string` | The mod lacks the permission named in the payload (for example `players:kick`). |
| `invalid-argument` | `string` | An argument was malformed; the payload says which one and why. |
| `limit-exceeded` | `string` | A size or count limit was hit (key too long, too many tasks, ...); the payload names the limit. |
| `stale-handle` | – | The handle refers to something that no longer exists (for example a player who left). |
| `unsupported` | – | The function is not available on this side or in this host version. |
| `internal` | `string` | The host failed for a reason the mod cannot fix; the payload is a human readable message. |
